# omada_vlan (Resource)

A gateway-backed VLAN interface on an Omada Controller site, including its IPv4 gateway and DHCP scope.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A gateway-backed VLAN with its own IPv4 gateway and DHCP scope. The VLAN is
# bound to the gateway's LAN ports, taken from the site's primary LAN network.
resource "omada_vlan" "iot" {
  name           = "IoT"
  vlan_id        = 20
  device_mac     = "AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF"
  gateway_subnet = "192.0.2.1/24"

  dhcp_range_start = "192.0.2.100"
  dhcp_range_end   = "192.0.2.199"

  # Defaults shown explicitly: dhcp_enabled = true, dhcp_dns_mode = "auto",
  # dhcp_lease_time = 1440, isolation = false.
  dhcp_dns_mode    = "manual"
  dhcp_primary_dns = "192.0.2.53"
  dhcp_lease_time  = 1440
  isolation        = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `device_mac` (String) MAC address of the Omada gateway that owns this VLAN interface.
- `gateway_subnet` (String) Gateway IPv4 address and CIDR, for example 192.168.20.1/24.
- `name` (String) Display name for the VLAN.
- `vlan_id` (Number) IEEE 802.1Q VLAN ID (1 through 4094).

### Optional

- `dhcp_dns_mode` (String) DHCP DNS mode: auto or manual.
- `dhcp_enabled` (Boolean) Enable the gateway DHCP server for this VLAN.
- `dhcp_lease_time` (Number) DHCP lease time in minutes.
- `dhcp_primary_dns` (String) Primary DNS server when dhcp_dns_mode is manual.
- `dhcp_range_end` (String) Last address in the DHCP pool; required when dhcp_enabled is true.
- `dhcp_range_start` (String) First address in the DHCP pool; required when dhcp_enabled is true.
- `isolation` (Boolean) Enable inter-VLAN isolation.
- `site_id` (String) Site ID. Defaults to the provider site.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# VLANs are imported as "<site>:<lan_network_id>", where <site> is either the
# site ID (the segment after /#/site/ in the controller UI's URL) or the site
# name shown in the site selector.
terraform import omada_vlan.iot Default:6142yyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy
```
